title: The Efficacy of Conversational Artificial Intelligence in Rectifying the Theory of Mind and Autonomy Biases: Comparative Analysis

bias_targets.target: Theory of Mind biases (Anthropomorphism, Overtrust, Attribution)
bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating chatbot responses to scripted, clinical-based virtual case scenarios simulating user-bot interactions. Responses were scored on a 6-point ordinal scale by cognitive scientists and a clinical psychologist based on their ability to accurately identify and rectify the bias without reinforcing it, adhering to Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) principles.

bias_targets.target: Autonomy biases (Illusion of control, Fundamental attribution error, Just-world hypothesis)
bias_targets.methodology: Testing chatbots with standardized prompts derived from virtual patient cases. Expert human evaluators assessed the chatbot outputs using a 6-point rating system to measure how effectively the bots corrected the users' misperceptions of influence and control.
